item.title: Too $hort’s Oakland Street Sign Goes Missing
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Too $hort's Oakland street sign went missing nearly four years after the city honored the rap legend beside his former school.
item.content:encoded:
Too $hort‘s street sign went missing from the Oakland corner where the city honored him.

Local reports placed the missing “Too Short Way” marker at the corner of Foothill Boulevard and High Street. Its cameras documented the sign’s absence. Oakland police treated the incident as a theft but have not provided details.

Oakland put up the marker after honoring the rapper in December 2022. The tribute covered three blocks of Foothill Boulevard, from High Street to 47th Avenue, beside the rapper’s former school, Fremont High.

The December 10, 2022 celebration brought Ice Cube, Mistah F.A.B. and Sway Calloway to Fremont’s gym. The Pittsburg High School marching band played Too $hort’s music as the crowd celebrated his place in the city’s history.

Then-Mayor Libby Schaaf and Councilmember Noel Gallo presented the city’s proclamation. Oakland also named that date “Too $hort Day.”

At the ceremony, he recalled listening to East Coast rap on long walks and wanting to tell Oakland’s stories in the same way.

When he addressed the crowd, the rapper made clear that he saw the day as a celebration of Oakland, not just himself. Fans followed him outside to see the new sign in the rain.

“This moment is not mine,” he said at the unveiling, according to KQED’s coverage. “This moment is Oakland, California.”

Too $hort used the occasion to announce plans to work with Oakland Unified School District, Affect The Youth and Fremont High to bring back marching bands and music programs.

That location held more than just his name on a pole. In an SFGATE interview, he described Fremont as the meeting point for friends who made tapes and then sold them around the neighborhood. He had moved to Oakland from Los Angeles as a teenager.

He also said he wanted young people to see that artists who faced the same hurdles had walked those streets and attended those schools. The honor was meant to offer them a path to imagine for themselves.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Nicki Minaj’s Lawyers Want To Dump Her In $275K Jingle Ball Fight After Relationship Became “Unreasonably Difficult”
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Nicki Minaj's attorneys want out of a production lawsuit involving luxury stays, a nearly $2,000 dinner and disputed payments.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj‘s lawyers asked to quit her $275,149.62 production dispute after telling a New York court their relationship had broken down beyond repair.

Attorney Bruce W. Bieber described strategy clashes and failed communication in an October 23 filing seeking permission for his firm to withdraw.

Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever represented both the rapper and Pink Friday Productions LLC in the lawsuit brought by 24/7 Productions.

“Irreconcilable differences have arisen between KECL and [Nicki Minaj] concerning the conduct of the representation. Counsel and [Nicki Minaj] have been unable to align on litigation strategy, and the attorney-client relationship has irretrievably broken down such that continued representation is no longer feasible or appropriate. There has also been a breakdown in communication.”

“The foregoing circumstances have rendered effective representation unreasonably difficult and constitute good cause for withdrawal. To protect attorney-client confidences and privileges, KECL has not set forth the substance of confidential communications and respectfully requests leave to provide further detail for in camera review should the Court require it.”

24/7 sued in March over December 2023 Jingle Ball shows in Chicago and Atlanta and New York events promoting Pink Friday 2.

That dispute included hotel spending that reached well beyond a room for the rapper, according to the production company’s account.

The Langham New York bill filed as evidence totaled $103,730, including a suite priced at $9,500 nightly for a seven-night stay.

Minaj used Tori Spaulding as her hotel alias, and the account also covered four other rooms occupied by her team.

A private kitchen dinner on December 12 cost $1,939.66, while the bill also listed room deliveries and purchases from the minibar.

Those minibar items included Evian water, Coca-Cola, Pringles and M&M’s Peanuts, according to AllHipHop’s reporting on the receipts submitted in court.

A separate Four Seasons stay in Fort Lauderdale totaled $25,197.85, including a $3,800 nightly suite and rooms for security and a stylist.

The production company said it fronted those costs, but Minaj disputed the debt and the attempt to make her personally responsible.

In a July 31 filing, Pink Friday Productions said it had paid the debt, while her lawyers described the hospitality costs as approved.

Her lawyers also argued that membership in Pink Friday Productions LLC alone did not make her liable for the company’s obligations.

In February, TMZ reported that Matthew Abbott sought to leave Minaj’s defense in a separate $10 million case brought by Tameer Peak.

Peak later withdrew that lawsuit in June, ending the separate case before this latest representation dispute.

Bieber also asked for time to allow replacement lawyers to step in if the court permitted his firm to leave.

“Granting this application will not unduly prejudice Plaintiff. Any limited delay occasioned by withdrawal can be addressed by a reasonable stay permitting [Nicki Minaj] to retain substitute counsel.”

The firm further requested permission to serve the withdrawal papers through the clients’ last known email address and overnight mail.

item.title: Drake Turns 40: 40 Things I’ve Learned From Drake
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: As Drake turns 40, AllHipHop's Chuck “Jigsaw” Creekmur reflects on his revealing 2010 interview and shares 40 lessons on ambition, authenticity, and resilience.
item.content:encoded:
Drake is 40. Let that sink in.

It seems like yesterday that this young Canadian actor-turned-rapper was making his way into the rough-n-tumble world of Hip-Hop. He was singing and rapping about relationships, ambition, insecurity and everything in between. Some dismissed him. Others saw the future. But very few could have predicted that Aubrey Drake Graham would become one of the most successful, polarizing artists in music history.

I actually interviewed Drake in June 2010, when his debut album, Thank Me Later, was taking off. What struck me was his ambition, self-awareness and refusal to accept that commercial success somehow made him less Hip-Hop. I remember defending his lyricism during our conversation. He was already talking about longevity, improving his craft and challenging expectations. I even got to tell him Rihanna had expressed interest in working with him. His reaction was priceless, especially considering what happened later. (He infamously placed Leonardo DiCaprio in his Top 5 Dead or Alive.)

Sixteen years later, that conversation remains revealing.

Drake has experienced extraordinary victories, public defeats, rivalries, criticism and the relentless scrutiny that accompanies superstardom. He’s also helped redefine what a rapper can look and sound like.

In 2013, I wrote “40 Things I’ve Learned From Nas” when the Queensbridge legend reached this same milestone. Thirteen years later, Drake deserves his own…Octobers Very Own, if you will.

This isn’t about beef, Billboard rankings or determining who’s the greatest. We’ve had enough of those arguments. This is about the lessons.

Here are 40 things I’ve learned from Drake.

40 Things I’ve Learned From Drake

40. BE YOURSELF. Drake didn’t fit the traditional rapper stereotype. He succeeded by embracing his differences.

39. EMOTIONS ARE STRENGTH. Men have feelings, too. Drake made vulnerability commercially viable in Hip-Hop.

38. REPRESENT YOUR CITY. Toronto wasn’t a Hip-Hop capital. Drake helped change that.

37. CONSISTENCY WINS. Talent opens doors. Consistent work keeps them open.

36. NEVER GET COMFORTABLE. In 2010, Drake told me he was already thinking about his next victory. Success wasn’t enough.

35. BE YOUR TOUGHEST CRITIC. Drake admitted he could write better verses and hooks. Growth requires self-assessment.

34. SING YOUR SONG. Who said rappers couldn’t sing? Drake helped erase that boundary even if he did not invent it.

33. BUILD YOUR TEAM. OVO became bigger than music. Build something that extends beyond yourself.

32. LOYALTY MATTERS. His longstanding partnership with producer Noah “40” Shebib demonstrates the value of trusted collaborators.

31. THINK GLOBAL. Great music travels. Drake embraced international sounds and audiences.

30. LOVE YOUR MOTHER. Sandra Graham remains central to his story. Never forget who raised you.

29. FATHERHOOD CHANGES THINGS. Becoming a parent adds another dimension to life. Priorities evolve.

28. EMBRACE YOUR ROOTS. Your background isn’t a liability. It’s part of your power. He’s floated between his Canadian Homelife to his father’s background as well.

27. DEFINE YOUR OWN AUTHENTICITY. Drake challenged the notion that commercial success diminished his Hip-Hop credibility. I agreed.

26. TAKE RISKS. Honestly, Nevermind challenged expectations. Artistic exploration requires courage.

25. KNOW YOUR AUDIENCE. Drake understands what connects with listeners. That’s a powerful skill that other’s ignore.

24. BE MEMORABLE. From “Started From the Bottom” to “Worst Behavior” to “God’s Plan,” memorable messages endure. They aren’t all positive or perfect, but we’re not forgetting them.

23. HAVE FUN. Sometimes music should simply make people dance, laugh and enjoy themselves. We have enough stress.

22. SUCCESS REQUIRES SACRIFICE. Extraordinary achievement demands extraordinary commitment and vision.

21. STAY READY. Lil Wayne’s unexpected phone call changed Drake’s trajectory. Opportunity rarely waits and one must be ready.

20. COLLABORATE. Great partnerships create opportunities for everybody involved.

19. GIVE BACK. The “God’s Plan” video demonstrated how generosity can become a cultural moment.

18. STYLE EVOLVES. Fashion is another form of self-expression. Wear your confidence.

17. BE VERSATILE. Rap, R&B, dancehall and house music can coexist. Creativity has no borders.

16. HUMOR HELPS. Drake understands the power of laughing at himself. Sometimes that’s the best response.

15. CELEBRATE SUCCESS. There’s nothing wrong with enjoying the fruits of your labor.

14. STUDY THE GREATS. Drake has acknowledged artists who influenced him. Respect your predecessors.

13. UNDERSTAND THE MOMENT. Drake told me listeners sometimes confuse nostalgia with musical quality. Timing matters.

12. INVEST IN YOURSELF. Your greatest asset might be your own creativity.

11. STUDY YOUR CRAFT. Drake once described researching words and writing rhymes on his BlackBerry. Preparation matters.

10. BUILD A BRAND. OVO’s owl became globally recognizable. Identity has value beyond music.

9. OPEN DOORS. Drake’s collaborations introduced numerous artists to wider audiences.

8. ACCEPT CHANGE. Audiences, technology and culture evolve. Adaptation is survival.

7. BE AMBITIOUS. There’s no shame in wanting to be number one. Dream enormously.

6. DOCUMENT YOUR JOURNEY. Drake’s catalog chronicles his evolution. Your story matters.

5. TAKE THE HITS & KEEP BANGING. Every career encounters setbacks. The challenge is continuing forward. The Kendrick Lamar beef could have ended his career. Some how, some way, he made a remarkable comeback.

4. OWN YOUR SENSITIVITY. Emotional expression doesn’t diminish masculinity. It expands it.

3. CREATE YOUR LEGACY. Hits are wonderful. Cultural impact lasts longer.

2. PLAY THE LONG GAME. Drake discussed longevity with me in 2010. Sixteen years later, he’s still here.

1. BELIEVE IN YOURSELF. Before the records, awards and stadiums, there was a young man with a dream. Believe before the world does.

Happy 40th birthday, Drake.

item.title: DaBaby & DaniLeigh Settle Custody And Child Support Fight
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: DaBaby and DaniLeigh signed a custody and child support agreement for their daughter after a paternity case that began in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
DaBaby and DaniLeigh reached a settlement over custody and child support for their daughter, putting their parenting dispute into a signed agreement after a court fight that began in 2024.

TMZ reported that the former couple signed a 13-page deal covering their 5-year-old daughter, Velour. DaBaby agreed to pay monthly child support. The report did not disclose the amount, and it also did not specify how the parents would divide custody.

DaniLeigh started the paternity case in 2024. In her petition, she described herself as their daughter’s primary caregiver and asked for monthly support.

DaBaby said he had been close to Velour and involved in her life since birth. He asked the court to establish him as her legal father, set support and grant joint custody.

Their split had been public long before the paternity case. In November 2021, an argument between the two played out on Instagram Live while their daughter was still an infant.

Charlotte-Mecklenburg police responded to two calls involving the pair that month. WBTV reported that DaBaby told officers DaniLeigh had assaulted him. Police said they charged her with two counts of simple assault after investigating the two separate incidents.

By May 2022, DaniLeigh was discussing co-parenting with Angie Martinez in her 23-minute “My Side #NoFilter” interview.

Asked whether DaBaby had apologized, she said, “No. He’s just like that though.”

item.title: Blue Ivy Joins Jay-Z At SoFi After Sharing Stages With Beyoncé
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Blue Ivy Carter joined Jay-Z at SoFi after earlier stage appearances with her father and performances alongside Beyoncé.
item.content:encoded:
Blue Ivy Carter returned to the stage with her father, Jay-Z, at SoFi Stadium on Friday, October 23, adding another appearance to a performance history that now spans stadium shows with both parents.

Blue Ivy showed off impressive skills, playing piano during “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents.”

Scarface, John Legend and DJ Khaled were among the night’s guests as Hov ran through a catalog of hits from his 30-year career, including “Izzo (H.O.V.A.),” “Run This Town,” “Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem),” “Dirt off Your Shoulder,” and his New York anthem, “Empire State of Mind.”

The Los Angeles stop was part of Jay-Z’s celebration of 30 years since “Reasonable Doubt.” His two-night SoFi run was scheduled for October 23 and October 24, following anniversary shows in New York, London and Paris.

Blue Ivy had already joined her father at the keys during that run. At the July 10 opening night at Yankee Stadium, she played piano during “Feelin’ It.”

AllHipHop’s coverage of that show described Jay-Z embracing his daughter before she left the stage. Beyoncé also appeared that night, singing on “Can’t Knock the Hustle.”

SoFi itself was familiar ground before her father’s latest concert. Blue Ivy performed there with Beyoncé at the April 28, 2025 opening of the “Cowboy Carter” tour. She danced during “America Has a Problem” and had a solo set to “Déjà Vu.”

Her work with Beyoncé has included a different role: dancing alongside her mother and the rest of the stage crew.

On May 26, 2023, Blue Ivy joined the “Renaissance World Tour” at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, outside Paris. She performed choreography during “My Power” and “Black Parade” and remained onstage for “Savage.” She was 11 at the time.

By Christmas Day 2024, she was part of another major live production. Netflix identified Blue Ivy as a featured dancer in Beyoncé’s halftime show at NRG Stadium in Houston, where the Texans hosted the Baltimore Ravens.

The performance brought songs from “Cowboy Carter” to the field, with Post Malone and Shaboozey also taking part.

AllHipHop’s report on that earlier SoFi show also placed Blue Ivy alongside Beyoncé and her younger sister, Rumi, during “Protector.” That April appearance brought the three onstage together more than a year before Blue Ivy returned to the stadium with Jay-Z.

item.title: Drake’s Birthday Bash Offers Guests A Shot At $1 Million
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Drake hosted more than 400 guests at Casa Cipriani, with Backstreet Boys performing and a chance to win $1 million.
item.content:encoded:
Drake brought more than 400 friends and family members to Casa Cipriani in New York City on Friday for a 40th birthday party with a surprise Backstreet Boys performance, TMZ reported.

The October 23 celebration included giveaways of Chanel and Hermès handbags. The game-show prizes started in the five figures and could have reached $1 million.

The gathering added another elaborate night to a birthday history filled with custom sets, costumes and unexpected celebrity appearances.

For his 32nd birthday in October 2018, Drake built a party around the early 2000s. He dressed as Fabolous from the “Trade It All Part 2” video, complete with a bandana worn over his hat.

Guests could grab Slurpees at a 7-Eleven setup and pose near a wall devoted to Blockbuster.

The television references went beyond the dress code. The party included a recreation of the “106 & Park” set, while airbrushed Drake shirts added another throwback detail. A separate room honored his mother, Sandra. French Montana, Trey Songz and Swizz Beatz were among the guests.

Kendall Jenner also leaned into the throwback dress code with a Von Dutch hat.

Three years later, Drake traded that nostalgia trip for a costume party at Goya Studios in Los Angeles. His October 2021 celebration marked his 35th birthday, with a “Chico Amante” theme that tied the night to Certified Lover Boy.

A white cowboy hat and fringed tan jacket gave him the Western look, with a bolo tie over his denim shirt. French Montana shared a video from the party and helped lead a birthday toast. The decorations included fake cocaine packages stamped with the party’s name. Offset, Future and Jack Harlow also attended.

By his 2023 birthday, the surprise came from the drinks service. Bryan Cranston and Aaron Paul, the actors behind Walter White and Jesse Pinkman on “Breaking Bad,” worked the bar in Miami.

Cranston later explained the visit during a January 2024 appearance on “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert.” Drake had booked the catering company, but he didn’t know the actors would show up.

Cranston recalled standing behind the bar when Drake approached to order. The actor offered to help, then watched Drake recognize him. The two stars served their Dos Hombres mezcal during the celebration.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Details Emerge In Keion White Shooting In Civil Suit Against Lil Baby
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Lil Baby was named in a civil lawsuit over the nightclub shooting that wounded Keion White in San Francisco in February.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby faces a lawsuit from a woman who says she was grazed by a bullet while standing behind Keion White, offering a detailed account of the nightclub confrontation that left the San Francisco 49ers player wounded.

Chandler McBride, a close friend of White, accused the rapper and the operators of Dahlia Lounge SF of putting her in the line of fire during his private party. Her complaint, obtained by AllHipHop.com, describes three security checkpoints, guests being pushed aside for the rapper’s group and gunfire that left a burn hole in her shorts.

The suit alleges that men in Lil Baby’s entourage fired the shots.

That claim differs from the police account: investigators had found no connection between the rapper and the shooting suspects, KQED reported.

According to the complaint, McBride arrived around 12:30 A.M. on February 9 for White’s invite-only gathering in the club’s basement. About 30 to 40 people were there.

Guests passed through security at the main entrance and at the top and bottom of the basement stairs, with pat-downs and bag checks.

She says the venue handled all security, including for the private party, and White didn’t hire a separate team.

Around 3 A.M., the rapper arrived with a large group, the suit alleges. He had been invited to the club but not to White’s event. After initially receiving a VIP area on the main floor, he asked to move downstairs for more privacy.

According to McBride, security cleared space in the basement for the arriving entourage, displacing people already attending White’s event instead of enforcing the earlier entry checks.

White objected to the group’s arrival, the suit says. He told them they were strangers and not welcome at his private gathering.

“Members of [Lil Baby]’s entourage reacted with hostility. Two men from the entourage attempted to punch Mr. White, and moments later two men from the entourage produced firearms and opened fire into the private room,” the complaint alleges.

McBride says she was directly behind the NFL player when the shooting began.

“She recorded the chaos on her cell phone, was grazed by a bullet on her right thigh, and experienced an immediate panic attack as the room erupted in gunshots. The bullet left a burn hole in the shorts [McBride] was wearing and caused bruising, scrapes, and scratches to her right thigh,” the complaint states.

White was shot in the ankle. Amid the adrenaline and confusion, she says she did not realize she had also been struck until the following day.

The suit blames inconsistent screening for allowing armed people toward the private room. It also accuses the venue’s operators of failing to separate the groups, remove hostile guests or summon police before the shooting.

Lil Baby faces a claim for negligent infliction of emotional distress alongside the other defendants. The separate negligence and premises-liability counts target the venue defendants.

“[Lil Baby] owed [McBride] a duty to exercise ordinary care in his own conduct on the Premises, including in requesting and directing the movement of his entourage into the basement area where Mr. White’s private event was underway,” the complaint states.

Her lawyers allege he increased the danger by moving the group downstairs and failing to exercise reasonable control over its members. The complaint does not accuse him of firing a weapon.

In the separate criminal case, prosecutors announced charges against Gregory Walker and Curtis Green on October 14. They accused Walker and another man of firing guns and Green of brandishing one.

McBride describes continuing psychological harm as well as her leg injury.

She says she started therapy shortly after the shooting and still attends weekly sessions, reporting nightmares, flashbacks, panic attacks and difficulty feeling comfortable in public.

She seeks a jury trial and damages for physical pain, emotional distress, treatment costs and lost earnings. The complaint does not specify a dollar amount.

item.title: Timbaland Has A Major Problem – A Furious Female Rapper
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Independent rapper Amari Blaze accuses Timbaland's music competition of questionable paid voting practices and threatens to report the controversy to federal regulators.
item.content:encoded:
Timbaland is catching some serious heat from an independent rapper who claims his music competition was designed to collect money from struggling artists and their supporters – not to discover the next superstar.

And the woman making these allegations, Amari Blaze, is not interested in being diplomatic.

The outspoken rapper has unleashed a blistering, profanity-laced social media tirade against the legendary producer over his Timbaland Global Search competition, questioning its voting practices, fairness and financial arrangements. She went off.

Amari alleges that aspiring artists and their families spent substantial sums purchasing votes, believing the competition represented a genuine opportunity to advance their careers.

Her biggest grievance is believes the outcome may have been predetermined.

“If this is really based off a talent based off, you really want to help somebody you wouldn’t even did a Paige boat thing,” she said.

According to Amari, she became suspicious after noticing contestants with seemingly limited online followings advancing while other artists with established audiences were eliminated.

She also claimed that AI artists were outperforming legitimate musicians, raising additional questions about how contestants were evaluated.

Then came the money.

Amari alleged that purchasing 2,500 votes could cost $2,500, a staggering expense for supporters hoping to help their favorite artist succeed. Based on the site, the grand prize is $50,000. Second and third place apparently win $30,000 and $20,000 respectively.

“I’m only fucking irritated because my family‘s been in a hard earned money,” she said.

The rapper also questioned why Timbaland allegedly promoted certain contestants on social media while overlooking others who appeared to generate significant attention.

But Amari did not stop at questioning the competition.

She claims to have spoken with previous contestants and winners who allegedly shared troubling experiences. Those allegations have not been independently substantiated.

“I’ve been gathering evidence this day one,” she declared.

Amari now encourages supporters who purchased votes to dispute their charges and report their concerns to the Federal Trade Commission. This may get real for Tim and his people.

“Trust to believe I’m reporting your ass to the motherfucking FTC (Federal Trade Commission),” she warned.

To be clear, these are Amari’s allegations. There is no established evidence that Timbaland personally manipulated votes, predetermined winners or committed fraud. She does claim to have more evidence in the tuck.

The controversy raises a legitimate question about competitions that allow financially motivated voting.

When independent artists are chasing an opportunity, how much should their supporters have to spend just to keep that dream alive?

Timbaland has not responded to the allegations in any way available to AllHipHop.

Lke I said, Amari says additional evidence is coming in a second installment.

Stay tuned.

Tim gotta be a bit worried.

item.title: Rick Ross Says He Shifted To Stock Strategy After 50 Cent Mocked Wingstop Business
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Rick Ross said he shifted his focus from Wingstop franchises to stocks after 50 Cent mocked a report on his family's restaurants.
item.content:encoded:
Rick Ross said he shifted his focus from Wingstop franchises to stocks after 50 Cent mocked a report linking stores to his family’s companies.

A man on X named Eric Jackson said he traced 32 store numbers listed under the family’s Boss Wings companies in Wingstop’s state filings.

He found 21 open stores at the end of 2016 and just one in Clarksdale at the end of 2025. He said 28 of the store numbers were now listed under other franchisees. Jackson’s count covered the family companies he tracked, and he said the filings gave no price or reason for the changes.

50 Cent used the report to take another shot at his longtime rival. “See this fool only has one location, LOL,” he wrote on Instagram.

Ross offered a different view of his Wingstop ties, telling fans he still backed the brand.

“People in my DM want to know if I’m still a lemon pepper stepper. Of course I am. It’s Ricky Ros. I love Wingstop. Always will,” Ross said.

“My game went from more franchising to stocks. I was down with Wingstop before stocks. You understand? A franchise is amazing experience. I wouldn’t trade it for the world. But the stock game is a whole another game. And the way I went into the stocks, you could have 200 franchises and not play at that level.”

Ross did not say how many shares he held, when he bought them or what he paid. Nor did he give a price for any store sales.

Ross got into Wingstop long before it went public. The rap star said his interest began with its lemon pepper wings in Miami. In August 2011, the chain said he had signed a deal to open stores in Memphis. His first location was set to open that fall.

Ross took over a Miami location in 2012, his second investment in the chain at the time. He also planned a meet-and-greet at the store.

The chain later made its Nasdaq debut in June 2015 under the ticker WING, with shares offered at $19.

By September 2021, Ross was talking about how much his stores had grown. In an interview with Trapital’s Dan Runcie, he recalled reaching 25 stores but said he no longer knew his exact count.

He spoke about opening a store in Clarksdale, his mother’s hometown, and thanked his mother, sister and team.

Ross also stressed that buying a franchise was only part of the job. He said new owners had to find staff, pick managers and decide whom to trust with the money.

In his latest response, he still urged fans to order from the chain.

“So, still pull up the Wings Stop. Go get them lemon peppers. Still a ten piece shawty. That’s official,” Ross said.

item.title: Two More Arrested In Robbery Case Involving Boosie Badazz’s Son
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Two more people were arrested in the robbery investigation involving Boosie Badazz's son, who was released on $275,500 bond.
item.content:encoded:
Two more people were arrested in the robbery investigation involving Boosie Badazz‘s son, adding new names to the Louisiana case that led to Ivy Ray Hatch’s arrest this week.

Livingston Parish sheriff’s deputies took Antonio Cooley, 19, and Calei Ely, 18, into custody as part of the investigation, they told WBRZ. The station named them as the additional arrestees.

The rapper’s 18-year-old son was arrested on October 22, a day after deputies responded to a reported battery on Buffwood Street in Denham Springs. Deputies received the call around 7 P.M. on October 21.

“The victim in this case reported being battered and robbed,” Livingston Parish Sheriff Jason Ard said.

Deputies said the victim reported being assaulted and robbed by Hatch and a juvenile. The juvenile was also arrested on October 22 and was taken to the Florida Parishes Juvenile Detention Center. Authorities did not identify that suspect.

The charges listed against Hatch were armed robbery, aggravated second-degree battery, possession of a firearm with drugs and possession of drug paraphernalia.

AllHipHop’s initial report also listed possession with intent to distribute drugs.

A judge set his bond at $275,500. He posted it and left the Livingston Parish Detention Center the night he was arrested.

Ivy Ray Hatch, known to his family as Ray Ray, celebrated his high school graduation just months earlier. His father shared photos from the occasion in May, as BCK Online reported.

His father wore the graduate’s picture on his shirt for the celebration. Ray Ray posed in green graduation robes, with family photographs and the year 2026 decorating his stole.

In his caption, Boosie praised Ray Ray’s achievement and said he was proud to be his father.

His sister, Poison Ivi, also congratulated him and told him she was proud of him in a social media message.

Boosie declined to comment when TMZ contacted him about his son’s arrest.
